What will be the output of the following program?

#include<stdio.h> 
int find(int *a, int n)
{

 return a[0];
 n--;

}
main() {
 int a[10] = {4, 10, 5, 6, 9, 3, 1, 20, 7};
 printf("%d\n", find(a , 10) );
}

int fun()
{
 int static x = 22;
 return x -= 2;
}

{

 {

}

 for (int i =0; i <2; i++)
 p = GOClasses(GOClasses(i));

In C language, the Order of evaluation of any part of any expression is unspecified.

That means if we have two functions $f()$ and $g(),$ in a single expression, then it is unspecified which one will be called first.

 int x = f(2) + g(3); 
// unspecified whether f() or g() is called first
